problem.text: Then it breaks on the server.

vm.text: A virtual machine pretends to be a whole computer.
A hypervisor splits the real hardware into VMs.
vm.say: A hypervisor splits the real hardware into V Ms.

vm.text: Each VM boots its own full operating system.
vm.say: Each V M boots its own full operating system.

vm.text: Strong walls, but heavy: gigabytes and minutes.

containers.text: Containers skip the extra operating systems.
They share the host’s kernel: one for all.
containers.say: They share the host's kernel. One for all.

containers.text: Linux namespaces and cgroups keep them apart.
containers.say: Linux namespaces and C groups keep them apart.

containers.text: Light: megabytes, and they start in a second.

compare.text: VMs isolate better. Containers pack tighter.
compare.say: V Ms isolate better. Containers pack tighter.

when.text: Need a different OS or hard isolation? Use a VM.
when.say: Need a different operating system, or hard isolation? Use a V M.

when.text: In the cloud, containers usually run inside VMs.
when.say: In the cloud, containers usually run inside V Ms.

workflow.text: A Dockerfile is the recipe; the image is the result.
workflow.say: A Docker file is the recipe. The image is the result.

workflow.text: Run the image, and you get a container.
